ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows square PQRS with Q at the upper left, P at the upper right, R at the lower left, and S at the lower right. Triangle RSU is drawn on side RS with apex U inside the square above RS. Triangle PST is drawn on the right side PS with apex T outside the square to the right. Reasoning: Since PQRS is a square and PQ has length 1, every side of the square has length 1. Use coordinates as in the analytic method: set R=(0,0), S=(1,0), P=(1,1), and Q=(0,1). Because RSU is equilateral on horizontal side RS with apex above RS, U=(1/2, sqrt(3)/2). Because PST is equilateral on vertical side PS with apex to the right, T=(1+sqrt(3)/2, 1/2). Then the horizontal difference from U to T is (1+sqrt(3)/2)-1/2=(1+sqrt(3))/2, and the vertical difference is 1/2-sqrt(3)/2=(1-sqrt(3))/2. Thus TU^2 = ((1+sqrt(3))/2)^2 + ((1-sqrt(3))/2)^2 = ((1+2sqrt(3)+3) + (1-2sqrt(3)+3))/4 = 8/4 = 2. Therefore TU=sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Coordinate/analytic route. From the image, identify the square with R bottom-left, S bottom-right, P top-right, Q top-left; triangle RSU is equilateral on the bottom side RS with apex U inside the square, and triangle PST is equilateral on the right side PS with apex T outside to the right. From the text, PQ=1 and PQRS is a square, so every side of the square has length 1. Place R=(0,0), S=(1,0), P=(1,1), Q=(0,1). Since RSU is equilateral with apex above RS, U=(1/2, sqrt(3)/2). Since PST is equilateral on vertical side PS with apex to the right, T=(1+sqrt(3)/2, 1/2). Compute TU by the distance formula: the horizontal difference is (1+sqrt(3)/2)-1/2=(1+sqrt(3))/2 and the vertical difference is 1/2-sqrt(3)/2=(1-sqrt(3))/2; squaring and adding gives 2, so TU=sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Pure angle/SAS route. From the image, focus on triangle SUT. The square has side length 1 because PQ=1, so RS=PS=1. In equilateral triangle RSU, SU=RS=1 and angle RSU=60°. In equilateral triangle PST, ST=PS=1 and angle PST=60°. At S, the square angle RSP is 90°. Because SU lies between SR and SP inside the square, the angle USP equals 90°-60°=30°. Because ST lies outside the square to the right and makes 60° with SP, angle PST=60°. Thus angle UST=30°+60°=90°. Therefore triangle SUT has two sides SU=ST=1 with included angle 90°, so by the Pythagorean theorem, TU=sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2).
